metadata.notes: Types, dates and density from the archive photographs and transport history (README, Vehicles and boats). Positions are plausible, not recorded: no particular cart or boat is documented here.

bridges.Pont d’Arcole: a footbridge from 1828; the iron road bridge opened in 1856 (works 1854-1856)
bridges.Pont Louis-Philippe: rebuilt 1860-1862; the earlier suspension bridge burned in 1848
bridges.Pont au Double: a footbridge before the cast-iron road bridge of 1883

types.note: Voiture à bras. Marville 1865-68 (rue Constantine, rue du Fouarre); Atget 1898 (quai aux Fleurs); a 'Location de voitures à bras' sign rue des Chantres in 1923 (Atget). End reasoned: rare after the 1930s.

Two-wheeled horse cart or tip-cart (tombereau). Marville 1858 (place du Châtelet); Atget: coal cart quai de la Tournelle, carts at the port de l'Hôtel-de-Ville, tombereaux 1913. Often unhitched, shafts down. End reasoned.
Covered cart with a canvas tilt (charrette bâchée). Marville 1865-68, rue Constantine and rue de la Cité.
Horse cab (fiacre, coupé), one horse. Atget c.1910: Compagnie générale des voitures cabs with taximeters; a cab rank on the quai Malaquais. Horse cabs dwindled in the 1920s; end reasoned.

Horse omnibus. Paris omnibuses from 1828 (Entreprise générale des omnibus); Compagnie générale des omnibus from 1855; upper deck (impériale) from 1853; last horse omnibus 11 January 1913. Marville 1858 (CGO office, Madeleine-Bastille omnibus), Atget 1898 (omnibus, place Saint-Sulpice).
Early motor car. Rare before 1900; an Atget view of the quai d'Orléans shows one parked (catalogued 1885-1925). Albert-Kahn 1917: a Renault parked on a quay.
Motor taxi of the Renault AG kind. Motor cabs with taximeters from 1905; the type was common until the later 1920s. Colours reasoned (red and black).
Early motor bus (Schneider kind). First CGO motor bus line in June 1906; Schneider PB2 buses from 1911 to the 1930s; green and cream (Albert-Kahn 1920, bus station place de la Madeleine).
Motor delivery van. Reasoned: motor vans replaced carts from the 1910s.
Mid-century car (Traction, 4CV, 2CV, DS shapes). Reasoned from the general history of Paris traffic.
Platform bus of the Renault TN kind: from the early 1930s until the last rear-platform buses in 1971.
Corrugated or rounded delivery van (Citroën H, 2CV van shapes). Reasoned.
Modern car. Reasoned.
Modern city bus. Many RATP lines cross the Cité (rue de la Cité, boulevard du Palais).
Modern van. Reasoned.
Péniche. Atget 1903 (quai des Orfèvres, quai des Célestins, quai des Grands-Augustins): wooden barges moored at the ports, often with a mast; today moored as houseboats.

Wash-boat (bateau-lavoir): open washing deck, drying loft above. Atget before 1906 by the pont Saint-Michel; Albert-Kahn 1914 (pont Marie) and 1923 (quai de Bourbon). The last Paris wash-boats went in the 1930s; end reasoned.
Floating baths (bains Vigier, bains de la Samaritaine): Atget c.1900-1910. End reasoned.
Steam river bus (bateau-mouche, bateau-omnibus): introduced for the 1867 Exposition universelle; the Compagnie des bateaux parisiens ran its last services in 1934 (approximate).
Small rowing boat: alongside barges and baths in Atget's views.
Glass-roofed sightseeing boat: bateaux-mouches again from 1949, landings at the square du Vert-Galant and the port de Montebello.
